Kuvaaja: hiihtäjän nopeus v ajan t funkt: Graph: the skier's speed v as a function of time t for two waxes. The points of wax A are black circles and the points of wax B grey squares. A separate rising straight line is fitted to each set of points. The line of wax A passes through the points (0 s; 2.10 m/s) and (8 s; 5.22 m/s), and its slope is 0.39 m/s². The line of wax B passes through the points (0 s; 1.90 m/s) and (8 s; 3.86 m/s), and its slope is 0.245 m/s².
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: hii: Two figures. On the left a picture of the situation: the skier glides upright down a snowy slope to the right, and a blue velocity arrow v points down the slope. On the right the skier's free-body diagram, with the skier as a rectangle tilted parallel to the slope: the weight G from the centre straight down, the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the slope and away from it, and kinetic friction from the upper corner of the lower surface up the slope. The components of the weight as dashed lines from the centre: G x down the slope and G y perpendicular to the slope and towards it; G y is as long as the normal force and G x is longer than the friction. Separately an orange acceleration arrow a down the slope. Axes: x down the slope and y perpendicular to the slope, away from it. The slope is drawn steeper and the friction larger than in the problem so that the arrows can be told apart.
Kaksi tilannekuvaa. Ylhäällä ennen törmä: Two pictures of the situation. At the top before the collision: car B comes from the left towards car A, which is at rest. Above car B there is a blue velocity arrow v B to the right and a purple momentum arrow p B to the right; the speed of car A is zero. At the bottom right after the collision: the cars are stuck together and move together to the right. Above them there is a blue velocity arrow v prime, which is shorter than v B, and a purple momentum arrow p prime, which is as long as p B. The positive direction is to the right. The arrows are to scale.
